walkthroughs.body_html:
Water & Aquatic Food Systems — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Water & Aquatic Food Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Water & Aquatic Food Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: They are larger than native species.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.

mcqs.q: Why are invasive species often more harmful than native species?
options: They lack natural predators or competitors in their new environment, so they spread unchecked.
Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
They are inherently more aggressive than native species.
They are larger than native species.
